script.analysis: Full19,008 canonical characters read in contiguous0-11000 and11000-19008 chunks. Sensory3:47am banking-app hook compares identical lives with different balances, then follows one hypothetical you through nine labeled levels. $0 damage-control Tuesday, $1K fridge screenshot/humor and reset, $10K mechanic call/sleep, $35K couch guilt and workplace bargaining, $100K Munger/compound mechanism, $250K Coast FIRE plus high-income counterstory, $500K market swings/hedonic treadmill, $1M anticlimactic coffee and Read story, $3M withdrawal/FIRE and enough. Bank-app muscle and Tuesday/couch objects recur, transitions tease next trap, and each level adds a psychological shift plus number. Final Heller anecdote reverses endless-level aspiration into enough and a one-week leak-reduction action. Emotional accessibility and continuity are observed; effects on retention unmeasured. Late stress-equality claim conflicts with earlier sleep relief and thumbnail; scenario guarantees and shifting measures compromise payoff. Original audio, cuts and visuals unverified.

claim_audit: The title promises savings and the opening calls the sole separating variable a savings-account number, but later tiers use liquid savings, 401(k), invested portfolio and household net worth interchangeably. Net worth subtracts debt and can include illiquid housing; it is not a spendable investment portfolio. Ages 24/25/28/32/36/41/46/52/55 are an illustrative path, not a verified longitudinal person or a prescribed schedule. No contribution ledger reproduces all endpoints; $1M at 52 reaching $3M at 55 needs substantial new capital or extraordinary returns, not merely continuing 7% growth.

Fed 2024 SHED says 63% WOULD pay a $400 expense with cash or equivalent, including a card paid in full next statement. The complementary 37% is not proof they CANNOT cover it. The 13% unable by any means is supported. Cash emergency ability is not zero net worth; 10% permanently at zero, 62% constantly paycheck-to-paycheck and Bankrate 59% need exact dates, definitions and denominators. Permanent poverty cannot be inferred from a cross-sectional share.

Princeton 2013 experiments support a context-dependent cognitive-performance effect comparable to 13 IQ points, not permanent IQ loss or a universal measured decrement for every poor person. The university explicitly distinguishes mental bandwidth from stress. The 62.1% medical-bankruptcy finding refers to a 2007 filer survey with broad medical/income-loss criteria; roughly three quarters insured at illness onset does not mean protected continuously or a current causal share of all bankruptcies. Exact 78% not independently recovered.

$1K at assumed 4% is $40/year, $3.33/month equivalent before tax; $10K is $400/year. These are variable-rate scenarios, not guaranteed fixed earnings or verified contemporary offers. $10K at assumed stock return 7% yields expected $700, not salary or reliable annual cash; principal can fall. $5K debt at 22% gives $1,100 simple annual interest only if balance and rate stay fixed. Keeping some emergency cash while repaying expensive debt is not inherently self-harm; the one-third doing exactly this joint behavior is unsupported.

$10K being three months implies $3,333 monthly essentials; $35K being eight months implies $4,375. Different ages may justify expenses changing, but the script provides no budget bridge. 55th-65th emergency percentile, 75th-85th liquid percentile, $35K plus unspecified 401(k) being average and top-5% $1.9M need dated weighted distributions, account definitions and age units. SCF median family net worth was $192,900 in 2022 dollars, with under-35 median $39K versus mean $183.5K. These are neither cash savings nor current individual ranks. A cross-sectional median below $500K cannot prove the median American NEVER reaches it across a lifetime.

The $12K/year, 7% route reaches $100K in 6.7919 years under a fractional extension of end-year annuity math, consistent with about 6.8; implied deposits roughly 81.5K (81.5%), not an exact monthly ledger. Monthly deposits with effective 7% annual give a different schedule. Return/contribution equality is $12K/.07 = $171,428.57, not a universal $100K switch. Returns can reverse and do not never stop/only accelerate. Munger quote date/wording not independently authenticated; $100K late-1990s equals about $200K in 2026 needs a specific month and CPI series, and future/full-year 2026 inflation is unavailable.

Only 40% of households EVER crossing $100K net worth is unsupported and conflicts with the 2022 family median $192,900 if meant as a contemporary population share. Lifetime ever rates are not identifiable from that cross section. Fidelity Q4 2025 mean 401(k) balance $146,400 broadly supports rounded $146K, but refers to its covered plans/participants, not every American or all assets held by a household. It does not establish a before-40 percentile.

$250K x 1.07^24 = $1,268,092 real at 65 from age 41, reasonably rounded $1.3M conditional on a constant 7% REAL return, no withdrawals, fees or taxes. A 7% nominal return instead produces a nominal figure needing inflation adjustment. Coast FIRE requires an expenditure target, future contributions/benefits, investment allocation and uncertainty analysis; $250K alone does not establish retirement is funded or that all further retirement saving is unnecessary. A mathematical expected-return scenario is not a guarantee.

3% of $500K is $15K; 25% is $125K, whereas 20% is $100K. Those are paper total-return changes, not guaranteed annual cash. The high-income Netflix couple and $2.18M couple are not independently identified/source-verified here; income does not guarantee security, but the absolute no raise big enough statement is not mathematically true for fixed spending. Couch guilt and every wealthy person anecdotes are neither representative samples nor proof that anxiety causes wealth.

$1M x4%=$40K/year ($3,333/month initial equivalent), $3M x4%=$120K/year ($10K/month), before account-specific taxes and expenses. Inflation-adjusted FOREVER is a materially misleading guarantee. Morningstar 2025 base-case research uses 3.9% initial withdrawal with annual inflation adjustment over 30 years at modeled 90% success, not perpetuity; 55-year-old retirement can be longer. Sequence risk, asset mix, longevity, fees and taxes matter. Withdrawing 4% of current balance each year is a different fluctuating-income strategy. Net worth containing a home cannot all fund withdrawals.

Pre-59.5 retirement distributions may incur ordinary income tax and generally 10% additional tax unless an exception applies; retiring at 52/55 needs an account-specific bridge and exceptions, not universal penalty-free access. Gross $120K withdrawal is not equivalent to net engineer salary, employment benefits or tax-free income. FIRE labels and fixed dollar bands are informal conventions, not official universal thresholds. $800K enough is a personal budget hypothesis, not a demonstrated target for all viewers.

Schwab original 2025 survey findings PDF page 4 supports $2.3M perceived wealth threshold; its dated sample was adults 21-75 surveyed Jan 27-Feb 7, with 2K nationally representative adults plus Gen Z oversample. This is a survey mean perception, not a minimum retirement need. Separate Schwab article reports $2.5M, so source/version matters. Exact 36% of millionaires feeling wealthy not established from this PDF. 18%/24M millionaire households, mean age61, daily millionaire creation, top7%/$3M and top1%/$15M lack matched definitions/source-year; individuals vs households and investable assets vs net worth differ.

Ronald Read is a selected success story, not the only true millionaire archetype or an investing trial. Hospital primary 2021 publication confirms an estate near $8M, but all clothing/food/holdings details and initial vs eventual bequest totals were not independently corroborated here. Treat the stored a TNT as possible ASR ambiguity, not a silently repaired company identity. The concluding Coast FIRE at 2 $150,000 is another stored-text inconsistency with the earlier $250K. Original audio unverified.

No identified study measures almost identical stress/cortisol at all nine wealth tiers. The $100K wealth cutoff for suffering relief is unsupported. The 2023 income/well-being research concerns annual income and heterogeneous emotional outcomes, not net worth or cortisol at a savings threshold; author abstract supports continuing income/well-being association for most participants. Full PMC retrieval hit a browser challenge, so no full-paper review claimed. This also contradicts the opening claim that only the account number separates poor sleep from sound sleep. Health, obligations, income security and individual circumstances can differ.
